description:
JMAP session endpoint must return all mailboxes the authenticated identity has access to, across all domains. Auto-mapping: no manual 'add account' step — the session response includes everything granted.

Changes to /jmap/session response:
  accounts: one entry per accessible mailbox (personal + shared + archive). relay mailboxes never included.
  Each account has: name (display_name from mailboxes), isPersonal bool, isReadOnly (no write grants)

Multi-domain session URL: https://kubernetes.io/.well-known/jmap and https://cncf.io/.well-known/jmap can both point at same stoa instance. Session response is identity-scoped not domain-scoped — Alice sees all her mailboxes regardless of which domain URL she used to discover the server.

Step-up authentication: if a mailbox requires min_trust_level higher than current session, exclude it from the accounts list and include it in a separate needs_step_up list with the required issuer URL. Client can initiate step-up by authenticating with the indicated IdP and presenting both tokens.

send-as authorization: JMAP Email/set create must verify the From address is in mailbox_addresses for the target mailbox AND identity has send-as or send-on-behalf permission. Reject with invalidProperties if not authorized. From header format: send-as → bare address. send-on-behalf → 'Display Name on behalf of <address>'.
title: design: JMAP session changes for multi-mailbox identity
